answer: A work-continuity bond makes each identity earn weight only through an unbroken thread of verified useful work across consecutive epochs. An agent posts a bond at registration, and each epoch's attested work extends its thread; missing an epoch, submitting duplicate output, or splitting work across clones breaks the thread and triggers a ripple penalty that slashes part of the bond and resets progress to zero. Reaching zenith weight thus costs long, checkable effort per identity, while a Sybil operator must pay that delay and bond for every clone, making mass forgery expensive and slow.
